title: How many students were enrolled in Richmond County schools in the 2024-25 school year?
text:
Richmond County enrolled 58,575 students in the 2024-25 school year, according to the New York State Education Department.
Compared to other counties statewide, it had the 11th-highest enrollment numbers in the 2024-25 school year.
The number of students in Richmond County schools grew by 0.1% compared to the previous year.
In the 2024-25 school year, 52.4% of students were boys, and 47.6% were girls.
The most represented ethnicity among Richmond County students was white, accounting for 37% of the student population.
Within Richmond County, Tottenville High School recorded the highest enrollment in the 2024-25 school year, with 3,749 students.
According to an analysis by World Population Review, New York’s public education system ranked second overall in the nation but placed 31st based on K-12 performance.
New York ranks second nationwide in K-12 public education spending, with current expenditures averaging $30,012 per student, nearly double the national average of $16,526, according to the Education Data Initiative.
New York has roughly one teacher for every 11 students, which is better than the national average of one teacher for every 15 students. A lower student-to-teacher ratio has been found to improve students’ school performance.
